content_pages.direct_answer: Usually not. If the bricks are still solid and the wall, steps, or walkway haven't shifted, deteriorated mortar can often be removed and replaced through repointing. The bigger question is whether the mortar is simply wearing out or whether the masonry itself is moving.

problems.name: Loose or damaged trim
problems.description: Baseboard, casing, or other interior trim that is loose, split, or pulling away from the wall.

problems.name: Wall mounting
problems.description: Mounting a television, shelf, curtain rod, or similar item where the homeowner wants it fastened securely.

problems.name: Worn door hardware
problems.description: A handle, lockset, hinge, or closer that is loose, worn, or no longer operating smoothly.

problems.name: Punch-list repairs
problems.description: A short list of small finish repairs after other work, or a set of minor items the homeowner wants handled together.

problems.name: Small carpentry repair
problems.description: A limited wood repair such as a shelf, casing return, or small section of trim — not a full remodel.

problems.name: Sunken pavers
problems.description: Patio or walkway pavers that have settled, rocked, or created a trip edge.

problems.name: Loose mortar
problems.description: Mortar joints that are cracking, receding, or falling out of brick or stone.

problems.name: Damaged brick walkway
problems.description: A brick walk that is heaving, broken, or uneven underfoot.

problems.name: Uneven stone patio
problems.description: A stone or paver patio surface that has shifted and is no longer a comfortable walking surface.

problems.name: Shifting retaining wall
problems.description: A low masonry retaining wall that is leaning, separating, or losing stones. Structural engineering is a separate question when movement is severe.

problems.name: Overgrown planting beds
problems.description: Beds that have filled with weeds, crowded plants, or spent growth the homeowner wants cleaned up.

problems.name: Landscape cleanup
problems.description: A yard that needs debris, leaves, or overgrowth cleared so the property is usable again.

problems.name: New planting beds
problems.description: A homeowner who wants beds edged, soil improved, and plants installed as a defined landscape project.

problems.name: Seasonal yard cleanup
problems.description: Spring or fall cleanup: leaves, cutbacks, and bed refresh rather than a full redesign.

problems.name: Worn interior paint
problems.description: Walls or ceilings whose paint is scuffed, faded, or ready for a fresh coat.

problems.name: Trim paint failure
problems.description: Window, door, or base trim whose paint is chipped or peeling while the surrounding walls may be fine.

problems.name: Paint after patching
problems.description: A wall or ceiling that has been repaired and now needs paint so the patch disappears.

problems.name: Hole in drywall
problems.description: A puncture, doorknob hole, or missing piece of drywall the homeowner wants patched.

problems.name: Ceiling drywall damage
problems.description: A ceiling that is sagging, cracked, or opened and needs drywall repair rather than paint alone.

problems.name: Unfinished drywall repair
problems.description: A patch that was started but not taped, coated, or sanded to a paintable surface.

problems.name: Cracked floor tile
problems.description: One or more floor tiles that are cracked and need replacement rather than a full floor redo.

problems.name: Loose backsplash tile
problems.description: Kitchen or bath backsplash tiles that have loosened or fallen.

problems.name: Bathroom floor tile repair
problems.description: Bathroom floor tile that is cracked, loose, or missing in a limited area.

problems.name: Cracked shower tile
problems.description: Shower wall tile that is cracked or loose. Waterproofing behind the tile is part of the project question, not something A5 diagnoses from a photo alone.

problems.name: Dripping faucet
problems.description: A faucet that drips or a handle that no longer shuts the water off cleanly.

problems.name: Running toilet
problems.description: A toilet that keeps running, refills constantly, or has a weak flush.

problems.name: Fixture replacement
problems.description: Replacing a faucet, toilet, or similar plumbing fixture as a planned project.

problems.name: Water heater replacement project
problems.description: A water heater the homeowner wants replaced or evaluated as a scheduled project rather than an urgent dispatch.

problems.name: Dead outlet
problems.description: An outlet that has no power or works intermittently.

problems.name: Faulty switch
problems.description: A switch that is loose, cracked, or no longer controls the light reliably.

problems.name: Ceiling fan project
problems.description: Installing or replacing a ceiling fan, including the question of whether the box and wiring can support it.

problems.name: Lighting update
problems.description: A planned change of lighting fixtures in a room or on a porch.

problems.name: Standing water
problems.description: A lawn or bed area where surface water sits because the grade slopes toward the house or a low spot. This is landscape grading, not a buried drainage system design.

problems.name: Light not working
problems.description: A light that does not work, flickers, or needs the fixture itself replaced.

problems.name: Pipe leak
problems.description: A leak the homeowner can see at a pipe, valve, or supply line. Not an emergency-dispatch promise.

problems.name: Drywall cracks
problems.description: A crack in a wall or ceiling that may be cosmetic or may need to be opened and retaped.

problems.name: Ceiling water damage
problems.description: A ceiling stain, bubble, or soft spot after a leak. The leak source, the drywall, and the finish are often separate parts of the same homeowner problem.

problems.name: Grout
problems.description: Grout that is cracking or washing out. This is a repair need, not a claim of specialty stone restoration.

problems.name: Sticking door
problems.description: An interior door that rubs, sticks, or no longer latches after seasonal movement or a loose hinge.

problems.name: Peeling paint
problems.description: Exterior siding or trim where paint is peeling, chalking, or failing and needs preparation before recoating.

problems.name: Recurring electrical issue
problems.description: A circuit, fixture, or device that keeps failing and needs a qualified electrical professional to look at the cause.

problems.name: Brick steps
problems.description: Brick front steps that are cracking, shifting, crumbling, or becoming uneven — a common masonry concern for Northern New Jersey homeowners.
